# Two tasks, one room
This fixture proves that one manager can hold two same-room task branches without conversation mixing. The exact records in `room.json`, `bonds.json`, and `manifests.json` are the evidence; the prose is only a guide to the joins.
- room: `task-auth-14`, tags `security`, `parallel-review` - task roots: `42` (`T-101`) and `57` (`T-205`) - manager: `mgr-dana`; branch owner: `sup-nova` - bonds: `b-20261109-0914-q4x7` → `sess-aa11`; `b-20261109-0917-m8k3` → `sess-bb22` - both assignment deliveries are `NEW`; each later reply/report is `REUSE`

## Required identity fields
Every manifest row records `send_id`, `attempt_id`, `target_session_id`, `profile`, `credential_scope`, canonical `request_bytes`, and `gateway_request_key`. The gateway key is scoped to the immutable endpoint and target, profile, and credential scope. An exact transport replay keeps the same attempt and key. A changed target, profile, or credential scope requires an authorized successor attempt and a new key.

## Branch routing assertions
```text bond key tuple #1 = (sup-nova, task-auth-14, 42, T-101) bond key tuple #2 = (sup-nova, task-auth-14, 57, T-205) manager thread #1 = mgr-dana/task-auth-14/42/T-101 manager thread #2 = mgr-dana/task-auth-14/57/T-205 session ids differ; thread roots differ; send targets match their own tuple ```
A manager review may cite both child report ids, but it cannot move a report from root 42 into root 57. The manager's parent report contains references, not a fabricated transcript. The branch fixture routes each child result to the manager thread named by its immutable `(room, thread_root, work_uid)` tuple.
